rationale: Closed one more checked lead and set up the next step. The snapshot-retention path looked as though a store configured with no retained snapshots would let FileSnapshotSink.Close reap the snapshot it had just finalized, before takeSnapshot recorded it and compacted the logs below it, leaving a node with neither logs nor a snapshot. The constructor rejects that configuration: NewFileSnapshotStoreWithLogger returns an error when retain is below one and the public constructor delegates to it, so ReapSnapshots always keeps at least the newest snapshot, and it reaps from the tail of a newest-first list. No defect and no record beyond this rationale, because nothing new was established. The next step I intend is the one limitation the verify account still carries: the caller's read of the FSM is not exercised, so the stale-read consequence is argued from the endpoint and the concurrent successor rather than shown. A probe can show it end to end by committing a value before the partition, letting the successor commit a different value, and reading the stalled leader's FSM after its verify returns success.
